Subject: Pilot qualification & recommended model slate — perf links & next steps

Hi Nora —

Thanks again for a constructive call today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can move towards a short pilot: 

Summary of fit and recommendations
- Primary user flows we heard: clinical note summarization (avg 800–1,500 tokens), extraction for downstream analytics, and an assist mode for clinicians (short prompts, high recall).
- Quality vs cost tradeoff: we recommend a two-model slate for the pilot to balance quality and unit cost:
  1) neox-20b (quantized) — primary candidate for quality-sensitive routes (higher token quality, lower hallucination on medical prompts). Redwood-verified perf profile: https://redwood.ai/perf/profiles/neox-20b-verified
  2) gpt-j-16k (quantized) — cost-efficient option for high-throughput batch summarization. Redwood-verified perf profile: https://redwood.ai/perf/profiles/gpt-j-16k-quantized

Performance highlights (Redwood-verified snapshots) — 2k context, typical production tuning:
- neox-20b (quant, fp16 kernels): TPS ~28 at concurrency 4; p99 token latency ~78ms (profile: see link above)
- gpt-j-16k (quant): TPS ~42 at concurrency 6; p99 token latency ~120ms

Attachments I will share in follow-up: prompt set we used for the call (promptset-axiom-v1.txt) and a short benchmark CSV with the exact run parameters (redwood-bench-axiom-2kcontext.csv).

Next steps / asks
- I’ll send the prompt set and the perf snapshot CSV (attached).
- Can you confirm the expected pilot traffic patterns (concurrency, tokens per request, % streaming vs full-response)? That will let us size Dedicated vs Hosted lanes.
- Would you like a short technical deep dive with Dev + Aditya next week to validate integration and security controls?

Proposed timeline
- This week: share bench and prompt set (by EOD Wed).
- Next week: technical deep dive (30–45m).
- Target: pilot kickoff week of 2026-11-08 if MAP and security checks align.

Thanks — I attached the files and included perf links inline.

—
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Grace / team / Nora — attaching the bench snapshot and a short notes file with the exact measurement methodology. Key points: 

- p99 numbers reported in the Redwood-verified profiles are token p99 for single-token emission latency under steady-state serving with KV cache enabled. End-to-end generation p99 depends on sequence length and generation length — we've included a small derivation in the CSV for the 2k-context summarization case (see the '2k_end2end_estimate' column).

Quick numbers from the attached run (2k context, beamless sampling, concurrency = production-like):
- neox-20b (quantized): avg TPS 28 at concurrency 4; token p50 ~18ms; token p99 ~78ms; end-to-end p99 for a 600-token generation (typical summarization length): ~550ms
- gpt-j-16k (quantized): avg TPS 42 at concurrency 6; token p50 ~28ms; token p99 ~120ms; end-to-end p99 for 600-token generation: ~1.1s

Cost delta (rough estimates, includes compute + Redis KV cache memory amortized):
- neox-20b: approx $0.00095 per input token-equivalent (quality lane)
- gpt-j-16k: approx $0.00062 per input token-equivalent (cost lane)
- For 1.2B tokens/month, delta ~ $384k/month in compute (neox higher); we recommend mixed routing: critical flows -> neox-20b; batch summaries -> gpt-j.

On-region controls:
- Logs/traces and token-level diagnostics can be kept in-customer-region (US-East) for Private/Dedicated customers; Hosted can be configured with regional retention and KMS-backed keys. Dev can run through specifics in the deep-dive.

Attachments included: redwood-bench-axiom-2kcontext.csv (CSV, 2.6MB) — contains the raw runs and derivations; promptset-axiom-v1.txt (12KB) — prompt variants; pilot-MAP-v1.pdf (PDF, 45KB) — 1-page MAP draft.

Links (for quick access):
- Bench folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AxiomBenchmarks
- neox-20b profile: https://redwood.ai/perf/profiles/neox-20b-verified
- gpt-j-16k profile: https://redwood.ai/perf/profiles/gpt-j-16k-quantized
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/HS-30912/deal/DEAL-AXM-427

LMK if you want any extra measurements (e.g., batching effects at concurrency 12 or different quant ops).
